answer: In an agent economy, a registry can force every new identity to lock a non-refundable bond that grows with the square of already-registered identities. One honest operator pays once, but a sybil attacker minting N fakes must front roughly N-squared in escrow, so flooding costs more than it can steal. To make identity tangible, the registry issues a sealed credential: a copper disc, its inlet notch stamped with the agent's unique hash, dyed umber so any re-stamp shows a black seam under UV. Duplicating that disc still requires the same bond, so forging one identity costs as much as earning it.
